main_text.p: Omnia tum animæ tum corpori necessaria,Iac.r. 17. Mat.6.33. quæ Dominus noster Iesus Christus ea precatione, quam nos ipse docuit, complexus est.
main_text.head: Quæ est illa precatio?
main_text.p: Pater noster{b}, qui es in cœlis, Sanctificetur nomen tuum: Veniat regnum tuum: Fiat voluntas tua, quemadmodum in cœlo, sic etiam in terra: Panem nostrum quotidianum da nobis hodie. Et remitte nobis debita nostra sicut & nos remittimus debitoribus nostris: & ne nos inducas in tentationem, sed libera nos à malo. Quia tuum est regnum, & po-tentia, & gloria, in sœcula. Amen.

head.i: Cur præcepit Christus, vt ita Deum compel-lemus, Pater noster?

main_text.p: Vt statim in ipso precationis exordio, conuenientem Dei filiis reuerentiam & fiduciam erga Deum in nobis excitet, quæ nostræ precationis fundamentum esse debet: nimirum, Deum propter Christum nobis patrem factum esse, & quę vera fide ab eo petimus nobis mul-* Mat. 7. 9. 10. 11.tò minùs negare, quàm parentes nostri nobisLuc. 11. 12. 13. bona terrena denegantc.

head.i: Cur additur: Qui es in cœlis?

main_text.p: Ne de cœlesti maiestate Dei humile quippiam aut terrenum {d}cogitemus: simul etiam, vt ab eius omnipotentia, quæcunq; animo & corpori sunt necessaria, {e}expectemus.
Sanctificetur nomen tuum, hoc est, Da principio[?] vt te recte {f}agnoscamus, & lucentem in omnibus

page.notes: The mark after "necessaria," is read as {a} and the mark after "noster" as {b}; both are uncertain. The note "Iac.r. 17." is printed as shown, with "r." where a 1 might be meant. The opening paragraph may continue from the previous page; this is not certain. The large initial P is read as a plain italic P. The reference marks in the text (c, d, e, f) are small superscript letters; the note letters follow the printed marks. The asterisk before the first marginal reference is printed in the margin and is not a text mark. The word after "principi" is set with a gap in the print; read as "principio" with a doubt mark.
